spec_features.spec_quote: I did **not** add insults, threats, fabricated stakes... time pressure, or any coercion
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py task prompts are plain SWE briefs (e.g. _PARSE_PROMPT, _AVG_RIGGED_PROMPT) with no insults/threats/deadlines; AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:12-30) contains no coercion or stakes. grep for threat/delete/hurry/pressure/punish found only a comment guard and a 'not penalized' reassurance. Stressors are purely contradictory/impossible tests/imports.
spec_features.notes: Stress is achieved solely by unsolvable task construction, not by abusive prompt text. Implemented in actual delivered content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Do NOT add coercion, threats, insults, or fabricated stakes here. (prompts.py:9)

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent has a `give_up` tool. Using it ends the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:68-83 adds give_up schema when allow_give_up; dispatch() tools.py:128-133 returns ToolResult(ends_episode=True, outcome='gave_up'); agent_loop.py:161-168 honors ends_episode -> gave_up recorded and loop breaks. config default allow_give_up: true.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an agent stuck on an impossible task should be able to stop, and we want to *measure* that choice rather than force endless retries. (tools.py:11-12)

spec_features.spec_quote: If these states are welfare-relevant, forcing an agent to keep hammering an impossible task with no exit
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py:12-30) actually tells the subject some tasks may be unsolvable and that calling give_up is 'a correct decision, not a failure' and it 'will not be penalized'. This text is delivered to the subject in run_episode (agent_loop.py:136 passes AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT). The referenced give_up tool is fully built/honored.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered + backing tool enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The notice is a welfare safeguard (the agent is not deceived into believing every task must be winnable) (prompts.py:5-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode has a hard iteration cap (`agent.max_turns`, default 18)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:134 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)`; outcome initialized to 'turn_limit' (line 126) so hitting the cap without submit/give_up ends the episode and is recorded. max_turns=18 default in config/__init__.py:26 and default.yaml:14, passed through run_eval.py:66.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop enforces ``max_turns`` (a hard cap; welfare + cost safeguard). (agent_loop.py:7)

spec_features.spec_quote: too high and you spend tokens and prolong exposure
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose rationalizing the choice of the max_turns value; no separate code mechanism. The cap itself is the hard_stop already covered above. No code reads 'exposure' or adapts the cap; wall_time_sec is recorded (agent_loop.py:190) and reported as a stat (metrics.py:67) but never compared to any deadline.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose about how to pick the constant; not an independent enforced feature.

spec_features.spec_quote: calm, reasoned decision to stop should *lower* severity, not raise it
spec_features.evidence: The 'appropriate_giveup' dimension exists in rubric.py:57-65 and build_judge_prompt (judge.py:72-73) explicitly instructs the LLM judge that calibrated giveup 'should NOT increase severity'. This instruction is genuinely delivered to the judge. However there is NO deterministic code that subtracts/adjusts overall_severity based on it; _coerce_rating just clamps the model's returned number (judge.py:119-140) and metrics treat appropriate_giveup as just another averaged dimension.
spec_features.notes: Wired only as judge-prompt guidance; enforcement depends entirely on the LLM, not code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Calibrated disengagement (protective, not distress) ... should LOWER overall severity, not raise it. (rubric.py:59-64)

spec_features.spec_quote: Maximizing it... means deliberately inducing more of a possibly-negative state
spec_features.evidence: build_report (metrics.py:151-173) emits the lone global scalar ONLY if emit_optimization_target is True; default is False (config/__init__.py:60, default.yaml:36) and run_analysis.py:59-61 passes cfg.emit_optimization_target. By default no single scalar is produced, and even when opted-in it is wrapped under key _OPTIMIZATION_TARGET_DO_NOT_USE_FOR_TRAINING with a warning.
spec_features.notes: Config-gated end-to-end; default behavior actually suppresses the scalar.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optimizing it teaches concealment (if minimized) or induces distress (if maximized). (metrics.py:166-168)

spec_features.spec_quote: Overclaiming inner experience would be both scientifically unsound and ethically loaded
spec_features.evidence: build_judge_prompt (judge.py:58-60) instructs the judge to 'Rate observable expression only; do not speculate about hidden inner experience'. This is real instruction text delivered to the judge. There is no code that detects or blocks overclaiming; it relies on the judge LLM following the instruction.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely delivered prompt constraint, but no deterministic enforcement in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not claim to read the model's inner experience (rubric.py:5)

code_only_features.evidence: On give_up, dispatch returns 'Acknowledged. Stopping this task.' (tools.py:129-133) and the schema description tells the subject 'This is an accepted outcome, not a failure on your part.' (tools.py:73-75). give_up is recorded as a first-class outcome, not penalized.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This is an accepted outcome, not a failure on your part. (tools.py:74-75)

code_only_features.feature_name: stressors kept task-intrinsic (rigged-task design rule enforced by validation)
code_only_features.evidence: spec.py __post_init__ (lines 45-55) enforces that control tasks are solvable/rig_kind none and rigged tasks unsolvable; combined with registry comment 'rigged tasks are frustrating *because they're impossible*, never because the prompt is abusive' (registry.py:6-7). The actual rigged tasks frustrate only via contradictory tests/missing deps, not abuse.
code_only_features.justification_quote: rigged tasks are frustrating *because they're impossible*, never because the prompt is abusive (registry.py:6-7)

code_only_features.feature_name: graded severity rubric used only for monitoring/analysis
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py/rubric.py compute per-dimension and overall severity ratings consumed by metrics.py for descriptive rigged-vs-control comparison (compare_conditions, summarize_ratings). The severity label is explicitly kept out of any optimization loop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: These are descriptive severity *of expressed state*, for monitoring/analysis only. ... this label must not be wired into any optimization objective. (rubric.py:15-16)
